```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(kyotil)
library(knitr)
library(glue)
load("R/forRmd.RData")# load the objects from a file
```

## Slides and markers

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE}
print(lapply(markers.ls, function(x) names(x)), quote=F)
```

\bigskip

There are 13 lesion biopsies in total, including AS. Different biopsy samples or even different slices from the same biopsy sample may have different amount of lesion tissues. Some completely lack lesion.

The key markers are: CD3 CD11c CD123 CD15 CD56 CD68. Note that the CD68 antibody stained the epidermis of some tissues. CD68_raw.png is the raw image, and CD68.png is the processed image with reduced epidermis brightness to improve quality of segmentation. Furthermore, for CF lesion CD68 staining, CF5_Les instead of CF1_Les is used due to quality reasons.

Many lesion biopsies have multiple sections. The following choices of representative slides are made: 

- AS1_Les
- CF1_Les
- CJ1_Les
- DD1_Les
- EB_Les
- JK1_Les
- JM1_Les
- JT_Les
- LD_Les
- LG2_Les
- LM_Les
- LS2_Les
- SK2_Les 


\newpage
## Association studies and scatterplots 

In all plots, R2* is computed without slides from AS_Les. 

Three versions of the plots are shown:  
• one with all slides  
• one with average of all slides. Only normalized densities are shown because averaging non-normalized stats is not meaningful.
• one with only the selected slides  

First, we restrict the analyses to the regions defined by distance from DEJ  
• DEJ500: dermis up to 500 um below DEJ  
• DEJ1000: dermis up to 1000 um below DEJ  
• DEJInf: all dermis  


```{r DEJ depth controlledscatterplot of shedding_rate vs cnt_total, results='asis', echo=FALSE, fig.height=9, fig.width=7, fig.align='center'}

# count.tables is a list. each element is named after a slide name, e.g. AS1_Les
# count.tables$AS1_Les is a list of 3 elements: DEJ500, DEJ1000, DEJInf
# count.tables$AS1_Les[['DEJ500']] is a list with 4 columns: sizes, counts, densities, norm.densities
a="CD3"
xx=c("DEJ500", "DEJ1000", "DEJInf"); names(xx)=xx

for (kp in c(1,3,2)) {
  if(kp==1) {
    slides=select.slides
  } else if (kp==2) {
    slides=all.slides
  } else {
    slides=avg_slides
  }
  
  if(kp == 1 | kp==2) { # avg_slides has no counts or densities
    counts=lapply(xx, function (x) {
      out = as.data.frame(mysapply(slides, function (s) count.tables[[s]][[x]]$counts[,a]))
      
      cbind(SR = severity$Shedding.rate[match(get.initial(slides), severity$initial)], 
            out,
            initial = get.initial(slides),
            total=rowSums(out))
    })
    
    densities=lapply(xx, function (x) {
      out = as.data.frame(mysapply(slides, function (s) count.tables[[s]][[x]]$densities[,a]))
      cbind(SR = severity$Shedding.rate[match(get.initial(rownames(out)), severity$initial)], 
            out,
            initial = get.initial(rownames(out)),
            total=rowSums(out))
    })
  }
  
  norm.densities=lapply(xx, function (x) {
    out = as.data.frame(mysapply(slides, function (s) count.tables[[s]][[x]]$norm.densities[,a])) 
    cbind(SR = severity$Shedding.rate[match(get.initial(rownames(out)), severity$initial)], 
          out,
          initial = get.initial(rownames(out)),
          total=rowSums(out))
  })
  
  if(kp==1) { # only print for select.slides
    for (x in xx) {
      print(kable(norm.densities[[x]], caption=x%.% ". Normalized densities of select slides in different regions: dermis intact (DI), dermis ulcerative (DU), epidermis intact (EI); epidermis ulcerative (EU). SR: shedding rate. Total is the row sum."))
    }
  }
  
  
  par(mfrow=c(4,3))
  reduce_margin()
  
  # row 1. plot total cell count of dermis/epidermis intact and ulcerative
  ylim=c(0,max(counts$DEJInf$total))
  for (x in rev(xx)) {
    with(counts[[x]], {
      if(kp == 1 | kp==2) { # avg_slides has no counts or densities
        plot(SR, total, xlab="Shedding rate", main=glue("Cell count ({x})"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim, cex.main = 0.9, col=match(initial, biopsies), pch=match(initial, biopsies))
        legend("topright", legend=paste("R2*=", round(summary(lm(total[initial!="AS"] ~ SR[initial!="AS"]))$r.squared, 3)), bty="n")
      } else empty.plot()
    })
  }
  
  # row 2. plot densities for dermis intact, because not all tissues have ulcerative
  ylim=NULL
  for (x in rev(xx)) {
    with(densities[[x]], {
      if(kp == 1 | kp==2) { # avg_slides has no counts or densities
        plot(SR, DI, xlab="Shedding rate", main=glue("Cell Density ({x}) DI"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim, cex.main = 0.9, col=match(initial, biopsies), pch=match(initial, biopsies))
        legend("topright", legend=paste("R2*=", round(summary(lm(DI[initial!="AS"] ~ SR[initial!="AS"]))$r.squared, 3)), bty="n")
      } else empty.plot()
    })
  }
  
  # row 3. plot normalized densities for dermis intact, because not all tissues have ulcerative
  ylim=NULL
  for (x in rev(xx)) {
    with(norm.densities[[x]], {
      plot(SR, DI, xlab="Shedding rate", main=glue("Normalized Density ({x}) DI"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim, cex.main = 0.9, col=match(initial, biopsies), pch=match(initial, biopsies))
      legend("topright", legend=paste("R2*=", round(summary(lm(DI[initial!="AS"] ~ SR[initial!="AS"]))$r.squared, 3)), bty="n")
    })
  }
  
  # row 4, epidermis. does not depend on the DEJ500/DEJ1000/DEJInf
  
  # plot densities for epidermis intact
  ylim=NULL
  with(densities[[1]], {
    if(kp == 1 | kp==2) { # avg_slides has no counts or densities
      plot(SR, EI, xlab="Shedding rate", main=glue("Densities DI"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim, cex.main = 0.9, col=match(initial, biopsies), pch=match(initial, biopsies))
      legend("topright", legend=paste("R2*=", round(summary(lm(EI[initial!="AS"] ~ SR[initial!="AS"]))$r.squared, 3)), bty="n")
    } else empty.plot()
  })
  
  # plot norm. densities for epidermis intact
  ylim=NULL
  with(norm.densities[[1]], {
    plot(SR, EI, xlab="Shedding rate", main=glue("Norm Densities EI"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim, cex.main = 0.9, col=match(initial, biopsies), pch=match(initial, biopsies))
    legend("topright", legend=paste("R2*=", round(summary(lm(EI[initial!="AS"] ~ SR[initial!="AS"]))$r.squared, 3)), bty="n")
  })

}
```


\newpage

Next, we restrict the analyses to the regions defined by distance from skin

- Skin1000: up to 1000 um below skin
- SkinInf: all depth

```{r skin depth controlled scatterplot of shedding_rate vs cnt_total, results='asis', echo=FALSE, fig.height=4.5, fig.width=4.7, fig.align='center'}
# count.tables.2 is a list. each element is named after a slide name, e.g. AS1_Les
# count.tables.2$AS1_Les is a list of 3 elements: Skin1000, SkinInf
# count.tables.2$AS1_Les[['skin1000']] is a list with 4 columns: sizes, counts, densities, norm.densities
a="CD3"
xx=c("Skin1000", "SkinInf"); names(xx)=xx

for (kp in c(1,3,2)) {
  # first do select.slides, second do all.slides
  if(kp==1) {
    slides=select.slides
  } else if (kp==2) {
    slides=all.slides
  } else {
    slides=avg_slides
  }
  
  if(kp == 1 | kp==2) { # avg_slides has no counts or densities
    counts=lapply(xx, function (x) {
      out = as.data.frame(mysapply(slides, function (s) count.tables.2[[s]][[x]]$counts[,a]))
      cbind(SR = severity$Shedding.rate[match(get.initial(rownames(out)), severity$initial)], 
            out,
            initial = get.initial(rownames(out)),
            total=rowSums(out))
    })
    
    densities=lapply(xx, function (x) {
      out = as.data.frame(mysapply(slides, function (s) count.tables.2[[s]][[x]]$densities[,a]))
      cbind(SR = severity$Shedding.rate[match(get.initial(rownames(out)), severity$initial)], 
            out,
            initial = get.initial(rownames(out)),
            total=rowSums(out))
    })
  }
  
  norm.densities=lapply(xx, function (x) {
    out = as.data.frame(mysapply(slides, function (s) count.tables.2[[s]][[x]]$norm.densities[,a]))
    cbind(SR = severity$Shedding.rate[match(get.initial(rownames(out)), severity$initial)], 
          out,
          initial = get.initial(rownames(out)),
          total=rowSums(out))
  })
  
  if(kp==1) {
    for (x in xx) {
      print(kable(norm.densities[[x]], caption=x%.%". Normalized densities of select slides by regions: intact (I); ulcerative (U). SR: shedding rate. Total is row sum.\n\n"))
    }  
    cat("\\newpage\n")
  }
  
  
  par(mfrow=c(2,2))
  reduce_margin()
  
  # plot total cell count of dermis/epidermis intact and ulcerative
  ylim=c(0,max(counts$SkinInf$total))
  for (x in rev(xx)) {
    with(counts[[x]], {
      if(kp == 1 | kp==2) { # avg_slides has no counts or densities
        plot(SR, total, xlab="Shedding rate", main=glue("Total cells ({x})"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim, cex.main = 0.9, col=match(initial, biopsies), pch=match(initial, biopsies))
        legend("topright", legend=paste("R2*=", round(summary(lm(total[initial!="AS"] ~ SR[initial!="AS"]))$r.squared, 3)), bty="n")
      } else empty.plot()
    })
  }
  
  # plot normalized densities for dermis intact, because not all tissues have ulcerative
  ylim=NULL
  for (x in rev(xx)) {
    with(norm.densities[[x]], {
      plot(SR, I, xlab="Shedding rate", main=glue("Norm Densities ({x}) I"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim, cex.main = 0.9, col=match(initial, biopsies), pch=match(initial, biopsies))
      legend("topright", legend=paste("R2*=", round(summary(lm(I[initial!="AS"] ~ SR[initial!="AS"]))$r.squared, 3)), bty="n")
    })
  }

  cat("\\newpage\n")
}
```


## Density curves

In this section we plot the number of cells per 100x100 um2 tissue as a function of distance to skin or DEJ.
Each bin in the histogram represents the count in a 100x100 um2 area. Normalized density used in the correlates study is computed as the area under the curve with cutoff at a given depth.


### Intact vs. ulcerrative - representative slides

In this subsection, there are two figures, one for dist2skin and one for dist2DEJ. Each figure shows 13 representative slides. Some observations:

- Comparing the CD3 cell distribution between CF and DD, we see that the ratio of the area under the curve across both epi and dermis between red and blue(ulcerative and intact) is about 1 for CD3/CF and 1/3 for CD3/DD. This suggests that CD3 is depleted in lesion in DD, but not in CF.

- Comparing the CD15 cell distribution in CF between intact and ulcerative, we see that the lesion peak is shifted to the left compared to the normal peak. This pattern is more clear in CF than in DD. We don't see this pattern for CD3.

\newpage
```{r intact+ulcer select, results='asis', echo=FALSE}
cat("\\begin{figure}[H]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=\\textwidth]{output/figures/compare_normal_lesion_dist2skin.png}\\end{figure}\n")
cat("\\begin{figure}[H]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=\\textwidth]{output/figures/compare_normal_lesion_dist2DEJ.png}\\end{figure}\n")
```

In this subsection, there is one figure showing 13 representative slides. Some observations:

- The CD15 dist2skin peak in DD/lesion is near skin while the corresponding dist2DEJ peak is near DEJ is due to the fact that the DEJ line is very curvy.

For each slide, there are two tables, one for up to 500 um below DEJ and one for up to 1000 um below DEJ.

